# `silk/machine/xstate`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

A `Definition` written as an xstate machine config, the JSON that xstate v6 reads with
`machineFromJSON` and that Stately Studio draws.

## Details
Every `on`, `always` and `after` entry is written as an array of transitions, which xstate
accepts for one transition too. A guard is written as an object whose `type` is the name
`Guards.named` gave it. A guard without a name gets the name `<state>.<event>`,
`<state>.always` for an eventless one. A tool shows the name, and the function stays in the
Silk source. The effects a row leaves are its `actions`, each an object whose `type` is the
effect as text. The reason of a `Chart.refuse` row is the `description` of its transition. A
`Chart.onDone` row is a transition on the event `xstate.done.state` that `matches` the id of
the state, as xstate v6 writes it.

[`Xstate.read`](#Xstate.impl.read) takes the same format back. It accepts a transition as a state name, as an
object with `target` and an optional `guard`, or as an array of those, and a guard as a name
or an object with a `type`, which are the forms xstate v5, xstate v6 and Stately Studio write.
A done transition is read from `xstate.done.state` or from a v5 `onDone`. A transition on an
event without a target takes the event and changes no state, which `Chart.stay` does, and the
event `*` is the transition that any event takes. The name of a guard and the `type` of each
action are kept. Context and other keys a `Definition` has no place for are left out.

A state with a history and child states is written with one more child, the history state
`hist`, whose `target` is the child state to enter when there is no history yet, and a
transition to the history targets `<state>.hist`. Reading takes any history child state as the
history of its parent, kept in the context field `last<State>`, and a target with a dot as a
transition to the history of the state before the dot.

## Errors
`XstateError` from [`Xstate.read`](#Xstate.impl.read) when the config has no `initial` state, has a part of the
wrong JSON kind, or names a delay that is not a number of milliseconds.

## Gotchas
xstate names the child states of a compound state but not the region that holds them. A
compound state `Red` is read as one region with the field `region` and the chart name
`RedRegion`. Each child state of a parallel state is read as a region whose field and chart
name are the child's key. Rename them in the definition before generating Silk source.

Import as `Xstate` with `import silk.machine.xstate { Xstate }`.
